What was a surprising good game?
Probably the recent DOOM game. After the delays, reboot and poor Alpha reactions, it seemed pretty grim. After playing it though, it's one of my favorite games of the year!
Yeah, DOOM was incredibly good. Favourite level for me would probably be the second boss fight, it was amazing.
The first time I played through it was so awesome. That second fight surprised almost as much as the last one.

Mad Max, I am a big Mad Max fan, I would feel fine even if it was an OK game, but it was very fun.

Shadow of Mordor too, sane reasons, and also the review copy shenanigans rose red flags, but again it is a fantastic game.

considering they are basically the same game. Yeah.

Down to the engine and the gameplay mechanics. Except one has cars.

Mad max was boring. Beautiful but boring. It plays like a Facebook time waster game. The action isn't great, the fights are formulaic.

It's stupid that max can literally walk right up to heavily fortified outposts and just walk in and beat the dozens of armed marauders with his fists.

A lot of potential in that game but holy fuck was it simple to the point of being insulting.

Yes they share mechanics, bit I felt like I was in each of those grabbed universes, Max felt much heavier Talion, but at the same time Talion felt like he had more battlefield experience. Both characters fought how you'd expect them to fight, Talion fought how you'd expect any LotR character to fight, while Max fought like what's you'd expect from him, much more brutal but not as elegant.

The car combat in Mad Max was also fun, AI not so good sometimes, like getting or if their car just to fight you mano-a-mano.

Shadow of Mordor's nemesis system is innovative and cool, I want to see it used more in games, made me feel like I had a history with the uruk-hai. Talion was a bit bland, the typical broody character, abs the main boas battles were pretty anti-climatic, but the game was fun to play.

Gonna go old school and say Saga Frontier. Going into it, I knew nothing except it had several story lines, all which had to be completed to finish. What I got was an RPG with one of the best leveling systems, good story, in depth character development, and heavy customization. An often overlooked PS1 gem

Tidalis, which is a match 3 style game developed by Arcen Games, the guys who developed AI Wars. It's really good fun, puts a good tweist on the match 3 genre, and has so many options and settings that you can have lots of different experiences, from an endless relaxation zen mode to a quick and fast adrenaline packed rush. You can make the game about reflexes and speed or you can make it about technical play with a more puzzly feel.

It also has a cool soundtrack.

I don't think it sold very well at all, which is a shame, but I've seen it on sale for under a dollar multiple times.

I recently played The Order 1886. I thought it was going to be a bad game considering the reviews. And definately somethings were really off. Like not being able to take out your gun while walking around. So even if you were wandering a dark tunnel, you knew you were somewhat safe because he wouldn't pull out his gun. Or like how he wouldn't shut off his lamp when he was trying to sneak around the tunnels knowing there's enemies close by.

I loved the boss fight QTE though. They were pretty fun if a bit challenging. The atmosphere and mood, once you got used to the game, helped set the mood for the game. But it played out more like a story than a game. And I thought it was brilliant. The fights did get repetitive, and the constant changing of main weapons bothered me. But, the game ended in a cliffhanger that I felt needed a bit more. So despite what reviews said, I enjoyed The Order and at 10 dollars it's a bargain.

Just sucks that it seems no sequel will ever be made since the game didn't do well.
I LOVED the setting. It's too bad that they weren't able to provide the value and length that people were looking for as I'll never get to see how it ends.
